content: The title of the page should be formatted as (Disease name) physical examination, with only the first letter capitalized. The purpose of this section is to provide a detailed description of the physical examination findings associated with the disease in question, focusing on how the disease may manifest during the examination. This section is not intended to explain how to perform a physical examination unless it involves specialized signs, such as Chvostek's sign, in which case a brief explanation may be included. It is acceptable to describe a physical examination finding commonly associated with a disease without additional elaboration. For example, in appendicitis, right lower quadrant abdominal tenderness is a typical finding. Unique physical examination findings that suggest specific aspects or complications of the disease should be mentioned, along with the context in which they may occur. For instance, rebound tenderness in appendicitis may indicate peritonitis. At the top of the edit box, include the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template. For example, if the term anterior spinal artery syndrome appears, the link should direct to the page for anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. Follow the prescribed format and capitalization guidelines as outlined in the template. The overview section should begin with the disease name in the first sentence and provide a concise summary of the physical examination findings. This section may mirror the physical examination segment from the overview page. Appearance of the Patient This section should describe the general appearance of a patient with the disease. If patients typically appear normal, state that they are usually well-appearing. Include physical descriptors such as obese, thin, cachectic, ill-appearing, or diaphoretic, and specify the clinical context in which these findings are observed. For example, patients may appear well in the early stages of cancer but cachectic in advanced stages. Findings may include: High-grade or low-grade fever. Hypothermia or hyperthermia. Tachycardia with a regular or irregularly irregular pulse. Bradycardia with a regular or irregularly irregular pulse. Tachypnea or bradypnea. Kussmaul respirations in advanced disease states. Weak, bounding, or paradoxical pulse; pulsus alternans; or asymmetric pulse. Skin Skin findings may include cyanosis, jaundice, pallor, or bruises. When describing a rash, include details such as color (e.g., erythematous), shape (e.g., flat or bullous), demarcation (e.g., well-circumscribed or diffuse), location (e.g., truncal, facial, or extremities), fluid content (e.g., vesicular, purulent, or clear), and odor (e.g., foul-smelling or odorless). HEENT (Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, and Throat) Abnormalities of the head or hair. Evidence of trauma. Icteric sclera. Nystagmus. Abnormal extraocular movements. Pupils non-reactive to light, accommodation, or both. Abnormal findings on ophthalmoscopic examination. Reduced hearing acuity. Abnormal Weber or Rinne tests (clearly specify whether the test is abnormal to avoid confusion). Ear canal exudate or tenderness upon palpation of the pinna or tragus. Inflamed or congested nares with or without purulent exudate. Facial tenderness. Erythematous throat with or without tonsillar swelling, exudates, or petechiae. Neck Jugular venous distension. Carotid bruits auscultated unilaterally or bilaterally using the bell or diaphragm of the stethoscope. Lymphadenopathy (describe location, size, tenderness, mobility, and symmetry). Thyromegaly or thyroid nodules. Positive hepatojugular reflux. Lungs Asymmetric or decreased chest expansion. Hypoor hyperresonance on percussion. Fine or coarse crackles at the lung bases or apices, unilaterally or bilaterally. Rhonchi. Vesicular or distant breath sounds. Expiratory or inspiratory wheezing with a normal or delayed expiratory phase. Egophony, bronchophony, or tactile fremitus (normal or abnormal). Heart Chest tenderness on palpation. Point of maximal impulse (PMI) within 2 cm of the sternum or displaced PMI, which may suggest specific conditions. Heave or thrill. Friction rub. Heart sounds (S1, S2, S3, S4). Gallops. Murmurs (describe grade, timing, and location, e.g., early systolic murmur best heard at the apex). Abdomen Abdominal distension. Tenderness in specific quadrants (e.g., right lower quadrant). Rebound tenderness (positive Blumberg sign). Palpable abdominal masses. Guarding. Hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, or hepatosplenomegaly. Positive findings on specialized tests (e.g., obturator test, psoas test, McBurney point tenderness, Murphy sign). Back Point tenderness over specific vertebrae (e.g., L3-L4). Sacral edema. Costovertebral angle tenderness (unilateral or bilateral), also referred to as Murphy's punch sign (distinct from Murphy's sign for cholecystitis). Buffalo hump. Genitourinary Palpable pelvic or adnexal masses. Inflamed mucosa. Penile or vaginal discharge (describe color, odor, and consistency; e.g., cottage cheese-like discharge in Candida vulvovaginitis or fishy odor in Trichomonas infection). Extremities Clubbing. Cyanosis. Pitting or non-pitting edema in the upper or lower extremities. Muscle atrophy. Fasciculations in the upper or lower extremities. Neuromuscular Orientation to person, place, and time. Altered mental status. Glasgow Coma Scale score. Presence of clonus. Hyperreflexia, hyporeflexia, or areflexia. Positive Babinski or plantar reflex (unilateral or bilateral). Muscle rigidity. Proximal or distal muscle weakness (unilateral or bilateral). Findings suggestive of cranial nerve deficits (e.g., dilated pupils indicating CN III deficit). Unilateral or bilateral weakness or sensory loss in the extremities. Positive straight leg raise test. Abnormal gait (e.g., ataxic, steppage, waddling, choreiform, Parkinsonian, or sensory gait). Positive or negative Trendelenburg sign. Tremors (describe type, e.g., resting or pill-rolling). Dysmetria or abnormal finger-to-nose test. Dysdiadochokinesia (e.g., abnormal palm-tapping test).
